referents.why: 'his hand' belongs to the subject of the verb, Aaron.
third feminine singular 'covered' takes the feminine singular frogs (w12) as subject.

links.why: a bare id naming a clause of the previous verse; 'then' does not cross verses.
Aaron stretches out his hand, repeating the verb of the earlier command 'stretch out your hand' as a report that it was carried out. The text has no pro-form, so medium.
links.category: report that a command was carried out

links.why: the frogs' coming up is what the stretching out brings about, so the link is a result, not a plain 'and then'.
the stretching out of the hand brings about the frogs' coming up.
a wayyiqtol continues the narrative line: the frogs came up and covered the land.

cant_tell.what: whether the frogs' coming up (cl1) fulfils the earlier command to bring them up (Exo.8.1 cl3)
cant_tell.why: its verb repeats the command's root, but the report is not a pro-form summary, so the rule for a clause repeating a command's verb does not clearly apply here.
